Low for short/simple work; medium for most work including agentic coding, with explicit checks; high for longer or stricter bounded work. xhigh/max need measured benefit versus Sonnet and can produce thinking without visible output.

Official 2026-09-28 launch: Code/apps default medium versus Platform/API high; medium well-specified and high harder agentic work; two max-vs-xhigh benchmark regressions are workload caveats, not universal rankings.

Efficiency-first Sonnet for everyday coding, analysis and tools; Opus for complex autonomous coding and broad refactors. Capability-first starting on Opus and highest-capability Fable guidance are vendor alternatives, not measured local profile equivalence. This page does not assign Sonnet effort.

claude-opus-5-5.notes: default_effort is the current medium starting setting, not the max/xhigh settings used in headline launch benchmarks. Benchmark settings do not override registered workload pins.

claude-fable-5-1.notes: default_effort denotes Claude Code and Platform/API high. Cowork and claude.ai default to medium. All values are surface snapshots, not observed installed controls. Mythos is excluded from active selection and custom profiles.

claude-sonnet-5-5.notes: default_effort denotes Platform/API high; Claude Code and Claude apps default to medium. Surface defaults do not change pinned agent profiles. Adaptive is the default; disabled/manual thinking is unsupported. Optional between_tools omits upfront reasoning at low/medium/high only; it accepts no display, budget_tokens or block_binding. Per-message effort changes require adaptive. These are API capabilities, not Claude Code settings. Retained role efforts remain unrun workload hypotheses after recalibration.

claude-haiku-5-5.notes: API disabled thinking is allowed at low/medium/high; xhigh/max require adaptive. Manual budgets are unsupported. Claude Code prevents disabling thinking for this model. API capability does not authorize a harness control. Medium is the starting setting; high is useful for longer/stricter work. Explicit checks prevent premature completion. xhigh/max are not default coding profiles and require measured benefit versus Sonnet.

alaa-implementer-haiku.rationale: Two distinct admissions: exact mechanical work with an exact transformation, exclusions, enumerated existing-file scope, expected result, settled design with no semantic discretion, known pattern and cheap discriminating checks; OR bounded semantic work with a settled local design or traced local cause, explicit expected behavior and invariants, finite owned scope, bounded local choices and a discriminating check. Every predicate of the chosen branch is required. File count alone does not decide. Reject ambiguous matches, undefined scope and interacting unresolved design. Medium may skip checks without explicit instructions; checks remain mandatory when specified. Unrun local user-authorized policy; vendor capability is not comparative calibration.
alaa-implementer-haiku.escalation_criterion: If the chosen branch loses an admission predicate, stop dependent work, preserve valid edits and return remaining work for reclassification; no scope or command-authority expansion. Interacting unresolved semantic/design decisions require Sonnet or Opus admission.

alaa-implementer-haiku-high.rationale: Longer or stricter bounded semantic implementation with a settled local design or traced local cause, explicit expected behavior and invariants, finite owned scope, bounded local choices and a discriminating check. Every predicate is required. Greater length or instruction-following demand supports high effort; interacting unresolved semantic/design decisions belong to Sonnet or Opus admission. No broader scope, authority or skipped checks. Unrun local user-authorized workload hypothesis; launch guidance is not comparative calibration.
alaa-implementer-haiku-high.escalation_criterion: If the chosen branch loses an admission predicate, stop dependent work, preserve valid edits and return remaining work for reclassification; no scope or command-authority expansion. notes: Active starting hypotheses use Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. Historical generations remain comparison snapshots only. No live calibration, account check, installation or runtime activation is implied; unavailable targets never silently fall back. Legacy replacement: every active selection request or routing reference to Haiku 4.5, including claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, selects the registered Haiku 5.5 role profile and its supported effort/thinking controls. If Haiku 5.5 is unavailable, report blocked to the lead; never select Haiku 4.5 or another fallback. Historical snapshots do not authorize active selection. Role selection follows workload evidence and the lightest admitted profile; vendor capability-first and efficiency-first recommendations are alternatives. Keep all local comparisons unrun; no mandatory paid trial ladder. Active Claude selection is restricted to Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1; Mythos is explicitly excluded, including custom profiles. Capability default_effort entries are qualified by model notes and source surface, not interchangeable runtime defaults.
